A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Genie Worksheets framework and retain corresponding experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, including the image-only user-study materials.

before.justification: v2 reports original STARv2 evaluations, a 62-participant user study, and repeated NeMo Guardrails experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations with additional language models, query-specific accuracy, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The worksheet predicates/actions, parsing, state updates, agent policy, and response generation are retained. v2 Figure 7 already shows the Python updates and Answer representation emphasized in v3. The Genie Runtime terminology and additional course knowledge-parser details do not establish a version-specific procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate STARv2 banking, trip, and trivia, plus restaurant reservation, ticket submission, and course enrollment. The additional model comparisons and analyses use this existing coverage; no new dataset, task, or population is established.

E2.justification: STARv2 Table 1 expands from four AnyTOD comparators to also include Llama 3.1 70B (FC), GPT-4o-mini (FC), and GPT-4 Turbo (FC). These enable direct comparisons with Genie's underlying models. The user-study GPT-4 baseline and appendix NeMo comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds Genie evaluation configurations using Llama 3.1 70B and GPT-4o-mini, zero-shot next-action prompting for the new STARv2 baselines, and an Answer-only evaluation subset. The retained user-study allocation, participant total, turn counts, and metric definitions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained conversation-length and semantic-error analyses, v3 examines dependence on the underlying LLM in Section 6.2 and isolates knowledge-query execution in Appendix R. Appendices P and S add banking annotation-error and user-correction case studies, substantially broadening the diagnostic questions examined.

E5.justification: Both versions report user-study t-tests at p < 0.05, shaded bands in the conversation-progress plot, and ten independent runs per NeMo query. Replacing significance asterisks with boldface changes presentation. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial cross-model results, including Genie plus GPT-4o-mini scores of 82.5/80.5/90.3 for bank/trip/trivia. Existing Genie/GPT-4 Turbo scores and user-study means remain unchanged. v3 additionally reports 93.75% Answer-only execution accuracy and latency measurements. Its Figure 5 also changes the accuracy-progress curves relative to v2 Figure 6.

T1.justification: The component mappings, agent-act definitions, policy logic, and metric formulas are retained or equivalently restated. Moving formal material into Appendices A, E, and J does not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The integrated knowledge/task framework and central user-study claims remain. v3 adds introductory claims about improvements across base LLMs and GPT-4o-mini approaching Genie/GPT-4 Turbo performance, while dropping v2's explicit claims to the first such language and representation.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive limitations concerning model capability, developer policies, few-shot examples, worksheet scaling, and cost/latency. Section 7.5 explains how explicit interpretations and confirmations support user correction, while Appendix Q discusses possible scaling approaches. These materially expand the qualifications surrounding the retained reliability claims.

D1.justification: Compared with v2's brief settings disclosure, v3 supplies STARv2 baseline prompts, model-provider information, the GPT-3.5 snapshot, course knowledge-parser tool interfaces, agent-creation instructions, and naming conventions. It also adds database dimensions, cost/latency information, and a project website. These substantially improve implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Llama 3, PET-SQL, CHASE-SQL, and reported chatbot failures, expanding the motivation and knowledge-query context. The main positioning against dialogue trees and LLM-based task-oriented dialogue remains, with softened explicit priority claims.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work moves forward, a separate architecture overview appears, and formal definitions, the policy algorithm, application statistics, and detailed metrics move into reorganized appendices with a table of contents.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws the architecture and update diagrams, annotates the worksheet illustration, and reworks both analysis plots. It expands and regroups Table 1, adds baseline-prompt tables, boxes code listings, and relocates retained tables and study screenshots.

improvement.justification: The new STARv2 comparisons better distinguish Genie's contribution from its underlying LLM, while expanded implementation details and substantive limitations improve reproducibility and assessment. These gains are tempered by unexplained changes to the accuracy-progress curves: v3 retains the 8%/43% decline narrative although its revised plot no longer supports those figures. The central user-study results remain unchanged.
